measurementPolicy: Only values traceable to published manufacturer specifications or confirmed public documentation are included. Grip-level dimensions (grip length, thumb reach, trigger reach) require caliper verification and are stored as null until measured. null = pending measurement, never an estimate.

ps5-dualsense.name: PlayStation 5 DualSense
fitNotes: Widest body in the mainstream lineup (160 mm) — generally comfortable for medium and large hands.
Symmetrical stick layout keeps both thumbs equidistant from center.
Weight 280 g is middle of the pack; lighter than Elite 2, heavier than Switch Pro.

ps4-dualshock-4.name: PlayStation 4 DualShock 4
fitNotes: Wide, flat body with short grips — a classic complaint from large-handed players.
At 210 g it is the lightest full-size controller here; easy on wrists during long sessions.
Same symmetrical layout as DualSense.

xbox-series.name: Xbox Wireless Controller (Series X/S)
fitNotes: Narrowest mainstream body (153.3 mm) with the deepest grips — the classic 'fits larger hands' reputation.
Asymmetric sticks place the left stick where the palm sits; right thumb reaches lower than on symmetrical pads.
286 g with AA batteries; slightly heavier than DualSense.

xbox-elite-2.name: Xbox Elite Series 2
fitNotes: Shares the Series X/S shell, so fit geometry matches the standard Xbox controller.
Heaviest mainstream controller (345 g) — premium feel, but tiring in long sessions unless you have strong grip.
Rubberized grips help limited-grip-strength players hold on with less force.
Elite Series 2 Core ($139.99) is the same shell with fewer accessories — identical fit.

dualsense-edge.name: PlayStation DualSense Edge
fitNotes: Same body geometry as the standard DualSense — if the DualSense fits, the Edge fits.
45 g heavier than the standard model due to swappable modules and batteries.
Swappable stick caps change thumb reach slightly (domed caps extend reach).

switch-pro.name: Nintendo Switch Pro Controller
fitNotes: Grip geometry is close to the Xbox family — deep grips with a narrower body.
At 246 g it is the lightest premium-feel controller; very forgiving on wrists.
Symmetrical sticks with comfortable reach for medium hands.

gamesir-g7-se.name: GameSir G7 SE
fitNotes: Hall-effect sticks — drift-resistant sensor tech (see reliability dataset).
Xbox-style asymmetric layout; retail pricing puts it near your stated $45 budget tier.
Body width pending caliper verification before we publish a fit verdict.

8bitdo-ultimate-c.name: 8BitDo Ultimate C
fitNotes: Budget Xbox-style layout with hall-effect sticks in the 2.4G version.
Light and compact — a reasonable first controller for small hands, pending dimension verification.
Body width pending caliper verification before we publish a fit verdict.

8bitdo-pro-2.name: 8BitDo Pro 2
fitNotes: Classic SNES-inspired symmetrical layout, very popular for emulation and fighting games.
Dimensions pending verification; verdict disabled until measured.

scuf-reflex.name: Scuf Reflex FPS
fitNotes: Licensed DualShock 4 shell — fit geometry matches the DS4 (161.2 mm wide).
Comes with interchangeable palm and grip assemblies for tailoring fit.
285 g measured in published reviews.

victrix-pro-bfg.name: Victrix Pro BFG
fitNotes: Unique modular layout — stick modules swap between symmetrical and asymmetric positions.
The only mainstream controller that can match either stick preference out of the box.
Dimensions and weight pending verification before we publish a fit verdict.

hori-pad-mini.name: HORI Pad Mini (Xbox / PS variants)
fitNotes: Officially positioned as a compact controller for smaller hands.
The PS variant keeps the symmetrical PlayStation layout; the Xbox variant is asymmetric.
Dimensions pending verification before we publish exact numbers.

logitech-f310.name: Logitech F310
fitNotes: Budget PC staple with a PlayStation-style symmetrical layout.
Wired only, no rumble — picked for compatibility, not fit.
Dimensions pending verification before we publish a fit verdict.

8bitdo-m30.name: 8BitDo M30
fitNotes: Sega Saturn-style six-button face, aimed at fighting and retro genres.
Small and light — a niche pick, not a general recommendation.
Dimensions pending verification before we publish a fit verdict.
